PASS WITH NOTES: PR #286, F199(c)
Head: d55bb57caf09a5fe7d7d3a16226a7e1f90a1b922

No in-scope exploitable vulnerability found under C33. All 16 changed files were reviewed read-only, including tests, docs and the ledger. One nonblocking rendering note remains; the pane-copy-safety check is not fully satisfied in the extension.

Checks

1. Report binding: crates/daemon/src/http/fyi.rs:300-310,383-385 resolves bound_seat before recording control context with the bound seat.id and seat.proc. Contradictory pane/native-session claims are refused by the existing binding helper. crates/daemon/src/reported_context.rs:216-228 returns a report only for the matching process incarnation. This is current-registration-strength binding, not independent authentication of the posting process; the same-user asserted-identity residual is accepted by C33.

2. Pane rendering: crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:3002 uses pij_core::directory::shell_word(pane), including apostrophe escaping. The daemon's warning is shell-safe. The extension refusal is different: .omp/extensions/pij/index.ts:479 passes process.env.TMUX_PANE, rust-runtime.ts:385 retains it, and rust-runtime.ts:1218 interpolates it without escaping or canonical %digits validation.

3. Delivery stays unchanged: crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:2969-3023 appends a warning after ordinary control admission. The report cannot suppress, reroute, authorize or alter the queued reload/new command. An old daemon's bare-422 retry in .omp/extensions/pij/adapters/daemon-http.ts:293-300 removes only control_context, retaining activity and binding fields.

4. Public privacy: no added real secrets, credentials, private owner/repository identities, private content or forbidden home paths found in the reviewed 16-file diff. Graded the current head and forward additions under C19/C21, not historical commits.

Nonblocking finding

S286-001, LOW, confidence 9/10: .omp/extensions/pij/adapters/rust-runtime.ts:1218 emits unescaped pane text in the refusal. Ordinary tmux %N values are inert and no incoming message/report supplies the pane. A shell-injection scenario would require a deliberately altered trusted local launch environment followed by copying the raw value into a shell; no normal-use or external-input path was identified. Under C33 this is local-env-only rendering hardening, not a merge block. Follow-up: use the existing shared shell-word escaping helper in this refusal. No additional review or mutation gate requested under C34.
